notes: Summary: PixelRill is a mid-market product analytics SaaS replacing an internal heuristics + single-model rerank pipeline. Primary drivers: reduce per-case latency for live support chat, lower token cost on nightly batches, improve result relevance for doc-search. They started with Hosted API evaluation to validate latency/cost and are now moving to a Dedicated POC to test production routing and runbook scenarios. POC scope: provision dedicated GPU pool (2-4 gpus), deploy primary model (open-llm-7b-ff16), and a quantized variant (open-llm-7b-4bit) for fallback. Canary plan: 5% of traffic to Dedicated during week 1, 25% week 2, 50% week 3, full cutover week 4 if KPIs met. Fallback routing: prefer primary variant in-region, automatically route to quantized variant if latency >250ms or failed inference; secondary fallback to hosted API (cross-account) for catastrophic capacity issues. Region failover: us-west primary, eu-west warm standby (replicated model weights and cached prefixes); if eu latency for EU users >350ms, route EU traffic to eu-west; if eu-west degraded, fail back to us-west with telemetry tagging. Rollback criteria: >5% error rate increase vs baseline, median latency regression >30% or cost per useful token >1.5x expected. Security: require SSO/SAML, customer KMS for secrets, audit logging for token access, data residency contract for EU records. Quotes / call snippets: "We need predictable SLOs for chat — sub-200ms p95 is table-stakes" (Raj, CTO). "If Dedicated only saves 20% on tokens but adds dev ops overhead we'll be cautious" (Head of Product). Open items: final SOW, approved VPC egress rules from security, dedicated pricing ladder for 4 GPU pool. POC deliverables: canary deployment, routing policies implemented, cost/perf report, rollback runbook.
